objects.description: A simple RAII-style wrapper around OpenSSL's MD5 context (MD5_CTX). It provides an interface to incrementally update the MD5 state with data, finalize the digest, and retrieve the resulting hash as a hexadecimal string via hex(). Construction initializes the context; update() feeds data; digest() finalizes the computation and populates _hex. After digest(), update() may be invalid unless the implementation re-initializes the context; this header does not specify reusability semantics.

functions.name: doris::Md5Digest::Md5Digest
functions.description: Constructs an MD5 digest helper that wraps an OpenSSL MD5_CTX. Initializes internal state so the instance is ready to accept data via update() and be finalized with digest(). Usage: create an instance, call update() zero or more times with data chunks, then call digest() and read the hexadecimal result via hex().
requirements: No special preconditions; object is ready for immediate use after construction.
Object is not thread-safe; do not access the same instance concurrently from multiple threads (inferred from typical mutable digest state).

functions.name: doris::Md5Digest::update
functions.signature: void doris::Md5Digest::update(const void* data, size_t length)
functions.description: Feeds a buffer of bytes into the MD5 computation. Can be called repeatedly to process data incrementally. Typical usage: call update() for each data chunk before finalizing with digest().
requirements: If length is greater than 0, data must be a valid, readable pointer to at least length bytes (inferred from pointer/length pattern).
The function does not take ownership of the buffer; the memory must remain valid only for the duration of the call (standard for such APIs; inferred).
Call update() only before calling digest(); behavior of calling update() after digest() is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: doris::Md5Digest::digest
functions.description: Finalizes the ongoing MD5 computation and produces the hex-encoded digest string stored internally. After calling this, hex() returns the computed digest. Typical usage: call once after all update() calls.
requirements: Should be called after all desired update() calls have completed (inferred).
Calling digest() multiple times or calling update() after digest() is unspecified; callers should assume digest() is intended to be called once per constructed instance (inferred).

functions.name: doris::Md5Digest::hex
functions.description: Returns a reference to the internal hex-encoded MD5 digest string. Intended to be read after digest() has been called. The returned reference remains valid as long as the Md5Digest object remains alive and its internal string is not modified.
requirements: Call digest() before calling hex() to ensure the returned string contains the final digest value; otherwise the contents are unspecified (inferred).
Do not use the returned reference after the Md5Digest object is destroyed (standard reference lifetime; inferred).

data_types.description: A byte buffer containing any sequence of bytes with no required structure or encoding. May include null bytes and non-UTF-8 data. Suitable for APIs that accept generic data blobs (pointer plus length).

import random
import struct
import zlib
import hashlib
from typing import List

# This generator creates arbitrary binary data that are valid inputs for
# doris::Md5Digest::update(data, length). The fuzz stub will sometimes pass
# length=0, otherwise it will use the full buffer size. Our goal is to
# provide diverse, interesting yet valid byte sequences to exercise MD5's
# incremental update paths and internal buffering (including various sizes
# and content patterns).

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# A set of interesting sizes to stress message length handling (including MD5
# block boundaries at 64 bytes and lengths around them), plus very small and
# larger sizes.
INTERESTING_SIZES: List[int] = [
    0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 47, 48, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 255,
    256, 511, 512, 767, 768, 1023, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4095
]

# Content builders that return bytes of the requested length.

def pat_repeating_byte(n: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b]) * n

def pat_incrementing(n: int, start: int = 0, step: int = 1) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start + i * step) & 0xFF) for i in range(n))

def pat_decrementing(n: int, start: int = 255, step: int = 1) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start - i * step) & 0xFF) for i in range(n))

def pat_alternating(n: int, a: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((a if (i & 1) == 0 else b) & 0xFF for i in range(n))

def pat_random(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def pat_ascii_text(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # English-like text with spaces and newlines sprinkled in
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 .,:;\n\t-_/\\"
    return bytes(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(n))

def pat_utf8(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build valid UTF-8 codepoints then truncate to n bytes (still likely valid prefix)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.6:
            # ASCII
            out.append(rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F))
        elif r < 0.8:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x800)
            out += bytes([(0xC0 | (cp >> 6)), (0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))])
        elif r < 0.95:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x800, 0x10000)
            out += bytes([
                0xE0 | (cp >> 12),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
            ])
        else:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x10000, 0x110000)
            out += bytes([
                0xF0 | (cp >> 18),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
            ])
    return bytes(out[:n])

def pat_structured(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix of small length-prefixed chunks and numeric fields to simulate structured data
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 8 < n:
        tag = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        # 50% fixed fields, 50% length-prefixed blob
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            val32 = rng.getrandbits(32)
            val64 = rng.getrandbits(64)
            out.append(tag)
            out += struct.pack('<I', val32)
            out += struct.pack('>Q', val64)
        else:
            blob_len = min(rng.randrange(0, 128), n - len(out) - 3)
            out.append(tag)
            out += struct.pack('<H', blob_len)
            out += pat_random(blob_len, rng)
    # pad to exact size with a checksum footer over current data
    remaining = max(0, n - len(out))
    if remaining:
        pad = pat_incrementing(remaining, start=rng.randrange(256))
        out += pad
    # overwrite last 4 bytes with a CRC32 to add deterministic structure
    if len(out) >= 4:
        crc = zlib.crc32(out[:-4]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        out[-4:] = struct.pack('<I', crc)
    return bytes(out[:n])

def pat_hash_collision_hint(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build inputs with common MD5 test vectors and variations repeated to fill length
    vectors = [
        b"", b"a", b"abc", b"message digest", b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz",
        b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789",
        b"1234567890" * 8,
    ]
    base = vectors[rng.randrange(len(vectors))]
    # Optionally prefix with count or metadata
    prefix = struct.pack('<I', len(base)) + base
    # Repeat and trim to desired length
    reps = (n + len(prefix) - 1) // max(1, len(prefix))
    data = (prefix * max(1, reps))[:n]
    # Occasionally append a 64-byte aligned pad of zeros
    if n >= 64 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_len = ((n // 64) * 64) - len(data)
        if pad_len > 0:
            data += b"\x00" * pad_len
    return data[:n]

PATTERNS = [
    lambda n, r: pat_repeating_byte(n, 0x00),
    lambda n, r: pat_repeating_byte(n, 0xFF),
    lambda n, r: pat_repeating_byte(n, 0x41),  # 'A'
    lambda n, r: pat_alternating(n, 0x00, 0xFF),
    lambda n, r: pat_alternating(n, 0x55, 0xAA),
    lambda n, r: pat_incrementing(n, start=0),
    lambda n, r: pat_decrementing(n, start=255),
    lambda n, r: pat_random(n, r),
    lambda n, r: pat_ascii_text(n, r),
    lambda n, r: pat_utf8(n, r),
    lambda n, r: pat_structured(n, r),
    lambda n, r: pat_hash_collision_hint(n, r),
]

def choose_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards interesting sizes but allow arbitrary range up to MAX_SIZE
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        size = INTERESTING_SIZES[rng.randrange(len(INTERESTING_SIZES))]
        return min(size, MAX_SIZE)
    # Otherwise pick a random size with slight bias towards smaller payloads
    # Use geometric-like distribution
    size = min(MAX_SIZE, int(rng.expovariate(1/256)))
    return size

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many concatenated segments to build. Concatenation allows
    # exercising multi-update-like variability even when the stub sends the
    # full buffer.
    segments = 1 + (rng.randrange(4) if rng.random() < 0.6 else 0)

    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total_len = 0

    for i in range(segments):
        # Pick size and pattern per segment
        size = choose_size(rng)
        # Ensure overall limit
        if total_len + size > MAX_SIZE:
            size = max(0, MAX_SIZE - total_len)
        # If no room left, break
        if size == 0 and total_len >= MAX_SIZE:
            break
        pattern_fn = PATTERNS[rng.randrange(len(PATTERNS))]
        seg = pattern_fn(size, rng)
        parts.append(seg)
        total_len += len(seg)
        if total_len >= MAX_SIZE:
            break

    data = b"".join(parts)[:MAX_SIZE]

    # Occasionally wrap with a simple header to simulate file-like inputs and
    # provide additional diversity for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME users too.
    # Header: b"MD5\0" + length(uint32 LE) + data + sha256(data) tail (16 bytes)
    # This is still arbitrary binary, and callers that ignore structure will
    # just hash the entire buffer.
    if rng.random() < 0.25 and len(data) <= MAX_SIZE - (4 + 4 + 16):
        header = b"MD5\x00" + struct.pack('<I', len(data))
        tail = hashlib.sha256(data).digest()[:16]
        wrapped = header + data + tail
        if len(wrapped) <= MAX_SIZE:
            data = wrapped

    return data
